title: Gaussian IMH samples and evaluates different proposals
evidence: For diagonal covariance [4], the sampler uses standard deviation 2 but proposal_logpdf(0) returns -2.305233 instead of -1.612086.
cause: The sampling branch takes sqrt(cov); the density branch passes cov directly as the normal scale.
impact: The Hastings correction is wrong, so the chain can target the wrong stationary distribution. This is not merely a normalization offset: the quadratic term also changes.
remedy: Use sqrt(cov) in the diagonal proposal density, and validate positive covariance.
regression: Compare dense/diagonal representations of the same Gaussian, including off-center densities and a stationary-moment test.

title: UKF sigma-point rules do not reproduce the input covariance
evidence: For P=[[2,1],[1,2]], Merwe and Julier reconstruct [[2.5,.866],[.866,1.5]]. The simplex rule reconstructs approximately 1.333 I.
cause: Lower-Cholesky rows are used as point displacements rather than columns. The simplex construction also does not have the claimed whitened covariance.
impact: Even the identity transform corrupts a correlated covariance; downstream nonlinear filtering and uncertainty estimates are wrong.
remedy: Transpose Cholesky displacements; construct and verify a centered, whitened simplex before applying the covariance factor.
regression: For every rule, reconstruct mean/covariance for random correlated SPD matrices at dimensions 1, 2, 5 and 20.

title: UKF observation update omits process noise from sigma points
evidence: Identity transition/observation, initial P=1, Q=1, R=1, y=1: UKF gives posterior mean .5 and covariance 1.5; the exact Kalman update gives 2/3 and 2/3.
cause: The prediction adds Q to cov1_, but observations and cross-covariance still use the pre-Q propagated points.
impact: Incorrect gains and posterior uncertainty even in a one-dimensional linear problem.
remedy: Regenerate sigma points from the predicted mean/covariance or implement a consistent augmented-noise UKF.
regression: Compare UKF to the linear Kalman filter for nonzero Q, correlated states and multi-step observations.

title: UKF log-likelihood is missing the Gaussian normalization
evidence: With Q=0, P=R=1, residual 1, reported log-likelihood is -.596574; the normalized value is -1.515512.
cause: The expression omits observation_dim * log(2*pi).
impact: Incorrect evidence/log-likelihood values, especially across models with different observation dimensions.
remedy: Include the normalization, or explicitly expose the result as an unnormalized potential instead of log_likelihood.
regression: Compare to multivariate_normal.logpdf in dimensions 1 and greater than 1.

title: UKF callable observation covariance is not evaluated
evidence: Providing observation_covariance=lambda t: eye(1) raises TypeError when an array is added to a function.
cause: Transition covariance callables are evaluated, but the observation covariance is passed through unchanged.
impact: Time-dependent observation noise cannot be used through the kernel.
remedy: Resolve callable observation covariance at the observation time, or reject it explicitly if unsupported.
regression: Compare constant-array and equivalent callable covariance over several times.

title: Pareto random samples have an extra location shift
evidence: For b=1, alpha=3, 20,000 draws have minimum about 2 and mean 2.4997; support starts at 1 and the mean is 1.5.
cause: jax.random.pareto already has support [1,infinity); adding one shifts every draw.
impact: Sampling disagrees with the distribution density/CDF/moments and biases any simulation using it.
remedy: Return samples*b; pin the random backend support convention with a regression.
regression: Check support, analytic moments with Monte Carlo tolerance, and CDF probability-integral transforms.

title: Generalized Pareto defaults are singular and support is not enforced
evidence: At the default c=0, PDF/CDF/SF raise ZeroDivisionError and PPF/ISF return NaN. At c=.5 and x=-1, PDF=8 and CDF=-3 instead of zero.
cause: Expressions divide by c without the exponential-limit branch and evaluate outside distribution support.
impact: Default construction is unusable for core probability operations; out-of-support probabilities can be invalid.
remedy: Implement stable c->0 limits and support-aware branches, including c<0 finite endpoints.
regression: Test zero, tiny positive/negative shape and both support boundaries, under JIT and differentiation.

title: Transformed CDF and quantile assume increasing bijectors
evidence: For transformed(norm(), lambda x:-x), CDF(1)=.158655 rather than .841345, and PPF(.9)=-1.281551 rather than +1.281551.
cause: CDF always uses the base CDF and quantile always uses q, without orientation handling.
impact: Wrong probabilities/quantiles for decreasing univariate transformations, even a negated standard normal.
remedy: Use a monotonicity contract to select CDF/SF and q/1-q; reject unknown orientation for these operations.
regression: Test positive and negative affine transforms, reversed support and CDF/PPF round trips.

title: Binomial CDF treats non-integer thresholds as continuous
evidence: Binomial(n=4,p=.5).cdf(.5)=.1604695 rather than .0625.
cause: The incomplete-beta formula receives k without first flooring it to a discrete threshold.
impact: The CDF is not the required step function; interval probabilities at fractional bounds are wrong.
remedy: Floor finite thresholds and retain correct behavior outside [0,n].
regression: Check equality of CDF(k+fraction) and CDF(k) across integer intervals.

title: Binomial entropy ignores the trial count
evidence: For p=.5, entropy is 1.386294 for both n=1 and n=4; correct values are .693147 and 1.407532.
cause: The formula is Bernoulli entropy plus log(2), with no dependence on n.
impact: Incorrect entropy-based objectives and diagnostics; degenerate probabilities also need zero-times-log-zero handling.
remedy: Implement a justified discrete summation/approximation with documented accuracy and endpoint handling.
regression: Test n=1, several larger n, p=0/1 and SciPy parity.

title: Poisson entropy can be negative
evidence: At rate=10, entropy is -13.025851 instead of 2.561410.
cause: The formula omits the expectation of log(k!).
impact: Invalid discrete entropy and incorrect entropy gradients.
remedy: Use a stable summation or a validated small/large-rate approximation.
regression: Test nonnegativity and reference accuracy across rates including zero.

title: Truncated normal delegates public methods to nonexistent backend APIs
evidence: PPF, ISF, mean, variance and entropy all raise AttributeError for a=-1,b=1 in both tested JAX versions.
cause: jax.scipy.stats.truncnorm does not provide those methods, although the wrapper calls them.
impact: Advertised distribution operations are unusable.
remedy: Implement stable truncated-normal formulas or make unsupported operations explicit until implemented.
regression: Exercise every public method against the installed supported backend, including tail truncations.

title: Default differential entropy and two alternative estimators are incorrect
evidence: On linspace(.001,.999,100), auto/Ebrahimi gives -3.735061 vs SciPy .008048; Van Es gives -1.436549 vs .063873; Correa gives NaN vs -.031353. Vasicek agrees.
cause: Ebrahimi uses adjacent gaps instead of the requested window gaps; Van Es takes logsumexp instead of the harmonic sum; Correa indexes an unpadded window.
impact: The default estimator is badly biased on a simple nearly uniform sample.
remedy: Implement each estimator from its defining window formula and add independent reference checks.
regression: Compare all methods on sorted/unsorted samples, axes, window lengths and large-n near-uniform data.

title: PCG is not invariant to right-hand-side scaling
evidence: For A=I and B=1e-4*ones((2,1)), PCG runs 200 iterations and returns about 4e-10 with relative residual .999996. The same problem at unit scale converges in one iteration.
cause: Valid small dot products are replaced with 1 using an absolute machine-epsilon threshold.
impact: Legitimate small systems fail. The large-operator Kalman solve currently discards PCG convergence diagnostics.
remedy: Use scale-aware breakdown handling that distinguishes valid nonzero denominators from zero/nonpositive curvature; propagate nonconvergence.
regression: Rescale identical SPD problems over many orders of magnitude and assert solution/residual invariance.

title: Lanczos logdet has a one-step dimension bug and an invalid exactness guarantee
evidence: logdet([[2]],num_steps=1) returns -33.845627 vs log(2)=.693147. Full two-step evaluation of [[2,1],[1,2]] returns 2.197225 vs log(3)=1.098612.
cause: One-step construction creates a nonempty off-diagonal and an unintended 2x2 matrix. Separately, one deterministic probe estimates a quadratic form, not an exact trace even at full Lanczos depth.
impact: Incorrect determinants and potentially biased large-operator Kalman likelihoods, whose default path uses this deterministic probe.
remedy: Fix tridiagonal sizes and breakdown; use explicit multi-probe stochastic trace estimation with accuracy diagnostics, removing the full-depth exactness claim.
regression: Test dimension/step=1, diagonal matrices, rotated SPD matrices and probe-averaged convergence.

title: Matrix structure predicates return wrong answers
evidence: An upper-triangular [[1,2],[0,1]] returns False with lower=False. A batch [I,2I] is reported [False,False] by is_diagonal_matrix.
cause: The upper branch omits the equality comparison; jnp.diag does not reconstruct a batched diagonal.
impact: Wrong dispatch/validation decisions for structured matrices; scalar tests do not cover batching.
remedy: Compare both triangular projections to A and construct batched diagonals using an identity mask with the requested axes.
regression: Cover upper/lower, batched, rectangular and non-default-axis cases.

title: Optional multistep solver module cannot be imported
evidence: Compiling the source raises SyntaxError: from __future__ imports must occur at the beginning of the file (line 34).
cause: Coefficient helpers were placed before a future import.
impact: Direct use of this optional module fails. Normal test collection succeeds because it does not import this path.
remedy: Move the future import to the top and ensure annotation types are defined.
regression: Compile all source files and smoke-import optional pure-Python modules.

title: Nested JIT loses stochastic sites and breaks log-joint evaluation
evidence: A one-site model gives {x: sample} when plain, but joint_sample(jax.jit(model)) returns {}. log_joint_fn of the jitted model raises AttributeError about .items. An explicit rv_p.bind reproduces it too; conditioning provides a passing control.
cause: The stochastic interpreter/reducer composition does not preserve site collection and state types across nested call/JIT boundaries.
impact: Common model compilation changes probabilistic transformation semantics.
remedy: Propagate the same stochastic visitor and compatible reducer state into nested jaxprs; test both high-level sampling and explicit primitives.
regression: Compare plain/JIT/nested-JIT joint_sample, trace, log_joint and condition for identical named-site programs.

title: Explicit transformer RNG is reused across dropout layers
evidence: A three-layer transformer forwards the identical key [0,8] to each dense dropout call.
cause: The supplied key is forwarded repeatedly without splitting/folding in layer and operation indices.
impact: Equal-shaped layers receive correlated dropout masks, unlike independent per-layer dropout. This affects the explicit-key path, not necessarily stored RNG streams.
remedy: Derive separate keys per layer and stochastic suboperation while preserving deterministic replay of a whole call.
regression: Check whole-call reproducibility and within-call mask independence with explicit RNG.

title: FlashAttention3 primitive implementations call undefined functions
evidence: The forwarding implementation raises NameError for _run_flash_forward_raw; _run_flash_backward_raw is likewise undefined. Static symbol checks confirm no definitions.
cause: The new primitive adapters reference missing raw forward/backward wrappers.
impact: The affected Flash3 backend cannot execute these implementations. GPU execution itself was not tested; the missing Python names were reproduced on CPU in both JAX versions.
remedy: Restore/import raw implementations and test eligible GPU forward/backward execution, not only backend availability guards.
regression: Add symbol/linkage smoke checks plus actual GPU forward/gradient tests.
